question: If capable AI becomes widely available, why would customers still choose your business?
measure: Compare work quality, total cost and human help for the same task.

moves.optimistic: Test one offering built around a delivered outcome. Keep human approval for consequential decisions and learn where judgement still matters.
moves.pragmatic: Choose one task that needs expert judgement. Compare AI assistance with your current process.
moves.sceptical: Build an advantage from useful tools and better organisational knowledge. Choose work whose value does not depend on an AGI deadline.

question: What would you change if your team could complete ten times as many routine cases?
measure: For each 100 cases, compare completed work, time spent on exceptions, recovery effort and customer outcomes.

moves.optimistic: Trial one bounded queue with a named owner, clear approval limits and tested recovery. Measure completed outcomes across the whole process.
moves.pragmatic: Choose one queue of repeatable tasks. Measure the current results. Then test AI help in stages, including difficult cases.
moves.sceptical: Make case owners faster with better context, drafting and triage. Keep responsibility clear and find which handovers cause the most rework.

question: If robots could do more physical work, where would you choose to operate?
measure: Measure useful operating time, human help, task changes, maintenance effort and safety.

moves.optimistic: Map one repetitive physical task, its exceptions and its safety boundaries. Define a small supervised trial before committing to a wider deployment.
moves.pragmatic: Choose one structured physical task. Identify any changes to its surroundings. Compare all operating costs with the current process.
moves.sceptical: Improve the process, sensing and existing automation first. Keep a clear test for when a general-purpose robot would add enough value.

question: If code were ten times easier to produce, what would still delay a useful release?
measure: Measure accepted changes, review time, defects found after release and recovery effort.

moves.optimistic: Test one path from a clear ticket to a reviewed release. Include monitoring and rollback so the experiment measures delivery, not just code generation.
moves.pragmatic: Choose one routine change. Define its tests and approval steps. Measure the whole path from request to monitored release.
moves.sceptical: Use assistance where results are easy to inspect. Work on the requirements, coordination and maintenance problems that remain after code is written.

question: If everyone had a personal tutor, how would you test what they had learnt?
measure: Measure what learners retain, how they solve unfamiliar problems and what they can do without help.

moves.optimistic: Pilot personalised practice for one defined skill. Agree how independent mastery will be assessed before expanding the learning programme.
moves.pragmatic: Choose one skill in an existing learning programme. Add AI tutoring. Compare later unaided results and teacher effort with the current approach.
moves.sceptical: Help teachers and mentors target their time. Test whether better preparation, feedback and practice improve learning within the existing programme.
